Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:10:1.hebrew: שקרנותיו קודמות לפרסותיו - דאמר מר: כל מעשה בראשית בקומתן נבראו, שור עם קרניו מגודלין, וכיון שיצא ראשו תחלה, נמצאו קרנותיו קודמות לפרסותיו:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:10:1.english: Whose horns preceded its hooves - For the Master said: All the works of Creation were created in their [full] stature, [meaning] a bull with its horns [already] grown. And since its head emerged first, its horns turned out to precede its hooves.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:10:2.hebrew: [ותיטב לה' משור פר - אמר דוד: ותיטב לה' תפלתי משור, שביום שהיה שור, דהיינו אותו יום שנולד, כדכתיב שור או כשב וגו', הרי עשוי ונגמר כפר שהוא בן ג', שאפילו מקרניו לא חסר]:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:10:2.english: [And it shall please the Lord better than an ox, a bull - David said: May my prayer please the Lord better than an ox, which, on the day it was an ox — that is, the day it was born, as it is written: "An ox or a sheep, etc." — was [already] formed and fully developed like a bull that is three [years old], so that it was not even lacking its horns].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:12:1.hebrew: רומי שעשתה קלנדא - תקנו אותו יום להקריב זבחים. וכל עיירות הסמוכות לה, לרומי, יודעין אנו שהן משתעבדות לה, לרומי, ליתן המס ולהביא להן כל צרכיהן, אבל אותן עיירות אין עושין קלנדא. מי הוי אסור לשאת ולתת עמהם, דנימא: הואיל ומשועבדות לרומי, יש לומר מה שהן קונין עכשיו יביאו לרומי להקריבן בני רומי:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:12:1.english: Rome that celebrated Kalenda - They established that day to sacrifice offerings. And all the towns neighboring it, [namely] Rome, we know that they are subjugated to it, [namely] Rome, to pay the tax and bring them all their needs, but those towns do not celebrate Kalenda. Is it forbidden to engage in business with them, reasoning that since they are subjugated to Rome, it can be said that what they purchase now they will bring to Rome for the people of Rome to sacrifice?

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:12:2.hebrew: או מותרות - הואיל ואין מקריבין הן, ואין יום איד זה שלהן:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:12:2.english: Or [are they] permitted - Since they do not offer sacrifices, and this festival is not theirs.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:12:3.english: To its worshippers - The people of Rome.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:13:1.hebrew: היא עצמה - כלומר, כל עצמה של איסור אינה אלא לעובדיה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:13:1.english: It itself - That is to say, the entirety of the prohibition applies only to its worshippers.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:14:1.hebrew: וסטרנליא וקרטסים - סיפא דבריית', וכולהו מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:14:1.english: And Saturnalia and Kratesis - [This is] the latter clause of the baraita, and all of them are explained below.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:14:2.english: An idolater - On the day of his son's feast, he worships [his] idol for having reached this [milestone].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:15:1.hebrew: אף אנן נמי תנינא - כרבי יוחנן, דעיירות המשועבדות מותרות:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:15:1.english: We too have learned [in a mishna] - [In accordance with] Rabbi Yochanan, that the subjugated towns are permitted.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:16:1.hebrew: אלא אותו האיש למעוטי מאי - פשיטא, דמי שלא גילח היום, ושאר עובדי כוכבים שלא עלו בו ביום מן הים, מותרין:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:16:1.english: Rather, "that man" [comes] to exclude what? - It is obvious that one who did not shave today, and the rest of the idolaters who did not come up from the sea on that day, are permitted.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:16:2.hebrew: אלא לאו למעוטי אנשים משועבדים - לאותו האיש, דמותרין, דלא אמרינן מאן דזבני ממטו ליה למפלח:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:16:2.english: Rather, is it not to exclude people subservient - To that man, that they are permitted, for we do not say that those who buy bring [it] to him to worship.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:17:1.hebrew: בטהרה - כלומר בלא כוונה, ואין שמים על לב:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:17:1.english: In purity - That is to say, without intention, and they do not pay attention.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:17:2.hebrew: וקרא לך - משמע שאתה קרוי לו, מעלה אני על אכילתך כאילו הוא מזבחו:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:17:2.english: And he calls you - This implies: Since you are invited by him, I consider your eating as though it were from his sacrifice.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:1:1.hebrew: ר' יהושע סבר ילפינן ממשה - להסדיר שבח תחלה, הלכך יתפלל י"ח תחלה, דאיכא שבח בתחלתן:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:1:1.english: Rabbi Yehoshua holds we learn from Moses - To set forth praise first; therefore, one should pray the Eighteen [Blessings] first, for there is praise at their beginning.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:1:2.hebrew: דרב גובריה - גדולת מעשיו וחכמתו רבה, ונאה לו לשבח ולהעדיף בשבחו של מלך מלכי המלכים, אבל איניש בעלמא מיחזי כיוהרא:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:1:2.english: For his might is great - The greatness of his deeds and his wisdom was great, and it was fitting for him to praise and to add [further] to the praise of the King of kings of kings, but [for] an ordinary person, it appears like arrogance.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:2:1.hebrew: מעין כל ברכה וברכה - אם היה משכח תלמודו, מאריך בחונן הדעת; אם בעל תשובה הוא, מאריך בהרוצה בתשובה; וכן כולן:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:2:1.english: Reflecting the nature of each and every blessing - If he was forgetting his learning, he prolongs [his prayer] in [the blessing of] "Who graciously grants knowledge"; if he is a penitent, he prolongs [his prayer] in [the blessing of] "Who desires repentance"; and so for all of them.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:1.english: And these are their festivals - That are forbidden [to engage in business] three days before them.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:2.english: Kalenda and Saturnalia - All of them are explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:3.hebrew: ויום הלידה - של מלך, עושין כל בני מלכותו יום איד משנה לשנה, ומקריבין זבחים:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:3.english: And the birthday - [The birthday] of the king; all the people of his kingdom make [it] a festival from year to year, and offer sacrifices.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:4.hebrew: שריפה - ששרפו עליו כלי תשמישו, כדרך המלכים:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:4.english: Burning - That they burned his personal utensils for him, in the manner of kings.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:5.hebrew: יש בה עבודת כוכבים - כלומר, אותו היום עובדין עבודת כוכבים, והוא להן יום איד, וכן משנה לשנה כל ימי בנו. ובכל הנך דחשבינן הכא, חשיבי ליה, ואסור ג' ימים לפניהן:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:5.english: [It] includes idol worship - That is to say, on that day they worship idols, and it is a festival for them, and likewise from year to year throughout all the days of his son. And in all of these that we enumerated here, they are important to him, and it is forbidden [to engage in business with them] three days before them.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:6.hebrew: אבל יום תגלחת זקנו כו' - שאין זמן קבוע לרבים, אלא כל אחד ואחד כשמגלח עושה יום איד:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:6.english: But the day of the shaving of his beard, etc. - For there is no fixed time for the public, but rather each and every one, when he shaves, makes [it] a festival day.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:7.hebrew: בלוריתו - כשמספר פעמים הרבה, מניח בלורית מאחריו, ומגלחה משנה לשנה, ויום שמגלחה, עושה יום איד:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:7.english: His lock of hair - When he cuts [his hair] many times, he leaves a lock of hair behind him [at the back of his head] and shaves it from year to year, and on the day that he shaves it, he makes [it] a festival day.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:8.hebrew: ויום שעלה מן הים - מקריב זבחים לעבודת כוכבים על דבר שניצל. ובכל הנך, אינו אסור אלא אותו היום, ולא לפניו ולא לאחריו, דלא חשיבי כולי האי:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:5:8.english: And the day he came up from the sea - He offers sacrifices to [his] idol for having been saved. And in all these [cases], it is forbidden only on that day, and neither before it nor after it, for they are not that significant.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:6:1.hebrew: אחר התקופה - היא תקופת טבת, והיו עושין ח' ימים רצופין איד, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:6:1.english: After the solstice - This is the solstice of Tevet, and they would observe eight consecutive days as a festival, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:6:2.hebrew: וסימנך - שלא תחליף לומר: קלנדא קרי אותן דלפני התקופה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:6:2.english: And your mnemonic - So that you do not switch [them], saying [that] it calls those [days] before the solstice 'Kalenda'.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:6:3.hebrew: אחור וקדם צרתני - אחור כתיב ברישא, מתני' נמי הנך דלאחר התקופה תנא ברישא:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:6:3.english: Behind and before You have hemmed me in - “Behind” [i.e., after] is written first; the Mishnah as well taught those [days] that are after the solstice first.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:7:1.english: The day progressively diminishing - From Tishrei until Tevet.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:9:1.hebrew: הא חזא ליה - יומי אריכי ביום תקופת תמוז, והיה לו לידע שמנהגו של עולם הוא:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 8a:9:1.english: Behold, he had seen - [He had seen] long days on the day of the solstice of Tammuz, and he should have known that it is the way of the world.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 8a:11:1.english: This is the reading of Rabbeinu Tam: "Makran is written" - For it did not appear to him that "makran" indicates one horn more than "makrin".

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 8a:4:1.hebrew: אם בא לומר אחר תפלתו אף כסדר יוה"כ אומר - משמע: אבל באמצע תפלתו — לא. ומה שנהגו עתה בתעניות ב' וה', שנוהגין להאריך בפסוקי דרחמי ובסליחות בברכת סלח לנו — איכא למימר: דציבור שאני, מידי דהוה אהא דאמרינן (ברכות ד' לד.) אל ישאל אדם צרכיו לא בג' ראשונות ולא בג' אחרונות, והא קמן שנהגו קרובץ בג' ראשונות; אלא לאו שמע מינה: דצבור שאני:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 8a:4:1.english: If one wishes to recite after his prayer, even like the order of Yom Kippur, he may recite [it] - This implies that in the middle of his prayer, [he may] not. And as for that which they are accustomed now on the fast days of Monday and Thursday, that they are accustomed to lengthen [the prayer] with verses of mercy and with *seliḥot* in the blessing of *Selaḥ Lanu* [Forgive Us] — one can say that a congregation is different. Just as it is with that which we say (Berakhot 34a): "A person should not request his needs, neither in the first three [blessings] nor in the last three [blessings]," and yet behold, before us they are accustomed [to recite] *kerovetz* [liturgical poems] in the first three [blessings]! Rather, is it not [correct to] conclude from it that a congregation is different?
